reason: The deck has a named caster slot, and the ball caster is its obvious fitting.
expectation: The caster will fit into the deck’s caster slot.

effect: The caster is fitted, and the deck accepts its remaining modules in any order. The two driven wheels will steer by turning at different speeds.
reaction: The explanation of steering without an axle is interesting.
reason: The rubber wheels and matched gearmotors look like the parts needed to make the wheel drives.
expectation: The wheels and motors will form the pair of drives for the deck.

effect: The wheels and gearmotors are now wheel drives, and their gearboxes trade speed for turning force.
reaction: The gearbox explanation makes the slower motors more meaningful.
reason: The assembled wheel drives match a named slot on the rover deck.
expectation: The wheel drives will fit into the deck’s wheel drives slot.

effect: The wheel drives are fitted alongside the caster; the electrical modules still need installing.
reason: The rover battery pack matches the deck’s named battery slot.
expectation: The battery pack will fit into the battery slot, with its connector parked and the switch off.

effect: The battery pack is installed; the switch harness and receiver remain to be fitted.
reaction: The installation is proceeding as expected.
reason: The switch harness matches another named slot on the deck.
expectation: The switch harness will fit into its slot, with the switch left off.

effect: The switch harness is fitted; the receiver remains to be installed.
reason: The receiver and motor driver match the deck’s named receiver slot.
expectation: The receiver and motor driver will fit into the deck.

effect: The receiver and motor driver are fitted, completing the deck’s listed slots.
reason: The gear guards appear to be the remaining protective parts for the installed wheel drives.
expectation: The guards will fit over the rover’s wheel drives.

effect: The rover is wired and guarded, with its wheels clear for testing; it now needs the remote.
reaction: The protected, wheels-clear test setup makes sense.
reason: The remote needs its batteries before it can control the rover.
expectation: The batteries will power the remote.

effect: The remote now has batteries and is ready to test with the guarded rover.
reason: The guarded rover is ready for its remote, and the remote now works.
expectation: The remote will control the rover’s wheels during the test.

effect: The remote test confirmed that the wheels respond independently, completing the chapter’s goal; radio carries instructions while the batteries supply energy.
reaction: Seeing the steering idea tested was a satisfying payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the rover with the remote brought the separate parts together and showed how independent wheel speeds can steer it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the electrical modules one at a time was straightforward but repetitive, with little new information in the individual results.

surprise.text: The explanation that two driven wheels and a free-turning caster can steer without a steering axle changed how I pictured the rover.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the named slots and the final guarded test gave the fittings a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the working rover gains a pen and draws invitations, though I would hope for more decisions than the repeated slot fittings.
